title: Substance case studies
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y10 lesson 6 (Substance case studies (pupil PDF, invented))
intro: Lesson 6: Substances: harms, the law and getting help. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Effects
points: Cannabis: memory, mental health, psychosis risk
Nitrous oxide: nerve damage, B12 deficiency

blocks.h: The law: Misuse of Drugs Act 1971

bullets: Class C: nitrous oxide (since 2023), some tranquillisers

panels.title: County lines
points: Gangs recruit young people to move drugs

passage.title: Case 1: Jake
paras: Jake, 15, is offered cannabis at a party and is told 'it's natural, so it's harmless'. A week later he is stopped by police with a small amount in his pocket.

passage.title: Case 2: Leah
paras: Leah, 16, is given new trainers by an older boy. Then he says she 'owes him' and asks her to carry small packages to another town on the train.

passage.title: Case 3: Sami
paras: Sami, 14, sees friends inhaling from silver canisters and balloons. One complains of tingling and numb feet.

questions.q: Case 1: what is the harm, what does the law say, and where can Jake get help?
questions.a: Harm: memory, mental health, psychosis risk. Law: cannabis is Class B; possession up to 5 years. Help: a parent, the safeguarding lead, Talk to Frank.

questions.q: Case 2: what is happening to Leah, and what should she do?
questions.a: County lines exploitation: gifts, then debt and threats. She is a victim; tell a trusted adult or the safeguarding lead; police can help (999 in danger).

questions.q: Case 3: what is the substance, the harm and the law?
questions.a: Nitrous oxide: nerve damage and B12 deficiency (the numb feet). Class C since 2023; possession up to 2 years. Help: tell an adult; see a GP.

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, write advice to a younger sibling about a 'free gift' from an older stranger. Start: 'If someone...'
questions.a: If someone gives you gifts and then asks for favours, it may be grooming for county lines; tell a parent or teacher.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain why the law treats supply more seriously than possession.
questions.a: Supply spreads harm to others and fuels crime.
B) Class B. Cannabis is Class B in the UK.

questions.q: Giving a friend drugs for free is... A) legal B) supply C) nothing
Big question: where could a young person get help with drugs or exploitation?
questions.a: Parents, safeguarding lead, GP, Talk to FRANK, Childline.
